newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA to boost cargo links with TAT.
newsitem.headline: BA to boost cargo links with TAT.

text.p: British Airways PLC said it plans to increase cargo co-operation with its French associate airline subsidiary, TAT European Airlines, later this month.
"From October 15, we will be carrying freight on TAT's daily Fokker 28 passenger service from Metz-Nancy-Lorraine airport to Lyon-Satolas," a Paris-based BA cargo official told Reuters.
The F28 can carry a maximum of 500 kilos of cargo.

On arrival at Lyon, shipments will be transferred on to British Airways' Boeing 737 passenger services to London/Gatwick from where they will be fed into the UK carrier's global cargo network, the official added.
"There will also be scope for shipments to be transferred on to Deustche BA's services from Lyon to Stuttgart," he said.
BA and TAT are targeting small-volume shipments - automotive parts, computer components and samples.
Earlier this year, BA began using TAT's daily F28 passenger service between Nantes and Toulouse as a feeder for shipments.
BA operates a scheduled 737 passenger service between London and Gatwick.

"Cargo co-operation between ourselves and TAT has taken some time to get going but we now we see things developing at a much quicker rate based on BA's savoir-faire and TAT's human and material resources," the official added.

TAT's Paris-Orly could emerge as a mini-hub for freight shipments brought in on its dense, domestic flight network, the official said. From Orly, shipments would also be transported to Britain on BA flights.
Longer term development could see a full-blown TAT domestic air freight product, he said.
